clue.text: Eccentric, but excellent, casserole

parts.note: crack as an adjective means first-rate, as in a crack shot
a pot is a cooking vessel, and a casserole is both the dish and what is cooked in it

explanation.surface: A food critic calls a stew both odd and superb.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crazy or oddball person, so the noun matches someone eccentric in the noun sense.

clue.text: Little light fish

definitions.meaning: first sense: a thin beam or glimmer of light
second sense: a flat cartilaginous sea fish such as the skate

explanation.walkthrough: A thin beam and a flat sea fish share one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a narrow beam of light and a flat-bodied fish related to sharks.

clue.text: Managed wearing a vestment

definitions.meaning: first sense: past tense of cope, got by
second sense: dressed in a cope, the long cloak worn by clergy

explanation.walkthrough: A cope is a long ecclesiastical cloak, so a priest wearing one is coped.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of a verb for getting by and an adjective for a cleric in a ceremonial cloak.

clue.text: In a pickle, choose a flower for hearing

indicators.note: for hearing says the phrase is spoken aloud to give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: pick a lily: pick is choose and a lily is a flower

explanation.surface: A puzzle about being in a jam and choosing blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pickle' looks like the idiom for being in trouble; 'In' is a link and a pickle is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a yellow mustard relish of chopped vegetables, a kind of pickle.

clue.text: Drink all round the place and fall over

indicators.note: the drinking word goes all round the abbreviation

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol heavily
PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone drinks all around town and keels over.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple is to tumble or fall down, losing balance.

clue.text: Intimate request followed by Hardy, quick

definitions.meaning: Nelson's dying words at Trafalgar are traditionally '..., Hardy'
a '... quick' hat is the classic British seaside novelty hat

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are phrases that complete the answer: Admiral Nelson's reported last words to Captain Hardy, and the slogan printed on cheap hats at British seaside resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words are a plea for a kiss, famously completed by Hardy in Nelson's case and by quick on seaside souvenir hats.

clue.text: Bird that flies without wings

definitions.meaning: first sense: a bird of prey
second sense: the paper toy flown on a string

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like a riddle, but it is just a description of the toy flown on a string.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fork-tailed bird of prey and a wingless toy held aloft by the wind.

clue.text: Very much depressed, man's time in game

parts.note: so low: feeling very down
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: A gloomy man spends his time playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Solo whist is a card game in which one player may bid against the other three.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a trick-taking card game, a variant of whist.

clue.text: Wise Men peer for moving ship

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift about, so Wise Men peer is rearranged

explanation.surface: The Magi look out for a sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A minesweeper is a naval vessel that clears sea mines.

clue.text: In the film I made, nothing short-sighted

indicators.note: the letter for nothing sits in the middle of the phrase for my own film

parts.note: my pic: a pic is a film, and one I made is mine
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A director admits their film had nothing in it worth seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical term for being unable to see distant things clearly, also used figuratively for lacking foresight.

clue.text: Peevishly irritable, but Clark not heartless

parts.note: Petula Clark is the British singer of Downtown

indicators.note: without a heart, the word not drops its central letter

parts.note: the word itself, which loses its middle

explanation.surface: A diva is cranky, though the singer Clark is not unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: Petula Clark is a British pop singer of the 1960s. NOT without its heart is NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant describes childish sulkiness and bad temper, the same as being peevish and easily annoyed.

clue.text: Diagnose the problem and criticise

definitions.meaning: first sense: literally locate the defect in a machine
second sense: the idiom meaning to complain or carp

explanation.walkthrough: A literal reading (locate the fault) and an idiomatic one (carp) of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally for a mechanic tracking down a defect and idiomatically for someone who nitpicks or complains.

clue.text: Manifestation in pink

parts.note: a pink is a garden flower of the carnation family

explanation.surface: Something shows up in a rosy colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Pink is the flower, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An incarnation is an embodiment or appearance of a spirit or idea in visible form.

clue.text: Coil up some rampant wisteria

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction to wind up the overgrown climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist something is to wind or curl it round on itself, as a coil does.

clue.text: Feeling poorly, having finished the last anagram?

definitions.meaning: first sense: the idiom for slightly unwell
second sense: sorts is a common anagram signal, so once it has been used up you are out of it

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a joke about crossword-setting: 'sorts' signals an anagram, and someone who has used the last one has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of sorts is an idiom for being mildly unwell or grumpy, the same as feeling under the weather.

clue.text: Anti-PC rioting that is irresistible to Tom

indicators.note: rioting suggests disorder, so the letters of Anti-PC are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A political rant about unrest among opponents of political correctness that someone called Tom cannot resist.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is not a person but a tomcat, a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a mint-family plant whose scent drives cats wild, so it is irresistible to a male cat.

clue.text: Change exercises after missing one class

indicators.note: the word for exercises is taken after it has lost the one

parts.note: trains means drills or exercises
I is the Roman numeral one
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Change your workout after skipping a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to alter completely, a strong synonym for change.

clue.text: Drink at home to end of bottle, face up on the floor

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
in means at home, as in 'stay in'

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of bottle

explanation.surface: Someone drinks at home down to the bottom of the bottle and ends up flat on their back.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying on one's back, face upwards, which is how someone ends up flat on the floor.

clue.text: Genuinely concerned with colleague

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely cares about a fellow worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Really means truly or in fact, a straight synonym for genuinely.

clue.text: Work on correspondence after the theatre

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it, so the work goes after the correspondence

parts.note: post is mail, letters received
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone deals with their letters after a night at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre here is the operating theatre, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-op means following a surgical operation, which takes place in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Rely on expending energy in part of pool

indicators.note: expending means using up, so the energy letter is spent and goes

parts.note: the deep end of a swimming pool
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Swimmers rely on spending effort in the deep part of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rely on' is the definition with 'on', since one depends on something; the parse gives just DEPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on something is to trust it or need it, the same as to rely.

clue.text: Planet Earth's last wetland

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of Earth, so the possessive ending is ignored

explanation.surface: A cosmic claim about the final wetland on our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh is low-lying waterlogged ground, a kind of wetland habitat.

clue.text: Carry on as salesman, coming back hard

indicators.note: the salesman is coming back, so the word rep is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
severe means harsh or hard

explanation.surface: A tough salesman keeps returning and won't give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, the same as to carry on.

clue.text: Take lead off vizsla wagging tail — essential

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and it is taken off vizsla
a wagging tail moves about, so the letters of tail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unclip the dog's leash; a Hungarian hunting dog wagging its tail is a must.
explanation.walkthrough: A vizsla is a Hungarian pointer. Its first letter V is taken, and TAIL is rearranged to ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means absolutely necessary, the same as essential.

clue.text: Tablet initially prescribed wrongly

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of prescribed

parts.note: ill as an adverb means badly or wrongly, as in ill-judged

explanation.surface: A doctor gave out the wrong medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a small tablet of medicine to swallow.

clue.text: Addictive substance reviewed in notice

indicators.note: to review is to look at again in a new way, so the letters of in notice are reworked

explanation.surface: A drug is examined in a public notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the habit-forming chemical in tobacco.

clue.text: Fat Pole carrying cask

indicators.note: the pole carries the cask inside it

parts.note: a rod is a pole, not a person from Poland
a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A fat Polish man lugs a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Pole look like a nationality; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means round and plump, a polite word for fat.

clue.text: Parasite found in genitals

indicators.note: the answer is found within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A medical note about an unwelcome bug in an intimate place.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is a louse egg or young louse, a parasite of the hair.

clue.text: I am interrupting fussily obstinate creature

indicators.note: the contraction breaks into the middle of the other word

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy
contracted, I am is I'm

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts a stubborn, pedantic beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lonely, fail to go back into romantic meeting

indicators.note: the reversed word goes into the date

parts.note: a date is a romantic appointment

indicators.note: the word lose goes back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: to lose is to fail, be defeated

explanation.surface: Feeling lonely after failing to return for a second romantic outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate describes someone forlorn and isolated, feeling abandoned and alone.
